# The problem {#sec-problem}

This document describes how each manufactured solution of the bidomain
equations used by cardiacFoam is built. In the method of manufactured solutions
[@roache2002code] the exact potentials are chosen first and the sources that
make them satisfy the equations are derived from them. The document gives the
exact potentials, the sources, the gauge of the extracellular potential and the
checks that each construction passes. It states the problems only; it contains
no solver output. Every displayed field, tensor, source and coefficient below
is printed by the sympy generator of its problem, `fda_bidomain_mms.py` or
`shell_bidomain_mms.py`, which also writes the NumPy reference module and, for
the shell, the C++ reference header of cardiacFoam. A reader with this document
and the generator folder can rebuild each problem in another code.

## Domain and governing equations

In the myocardium $\Omega_H\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, with sealed
boundary $\Gamma_N=\partial\Omega_H$ and outward unit normal $\mathbf n$, the
bidomain equations for the intracellular and extracellular potentials
$\phi_i$, $\phi_e$ and the transmembrane potential $V_m=\phi_i-\phi_e$ are

$$
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\chi C_m \frac{\partial V_m}{\partial t}
&=\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i\right)
-\chi C_m I_{\mathrm{ion}}+I_{\mathrm{app}}
&&\text{in }\Omega_H,\\
0&=\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i\right)
+\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla\phi_e\right)-s_e
&&\text{in }\Omega_H,\\
\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i=0,\quad
\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla\phi_e&=0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_N,
\end{aligned}
\right.
$$

with the ionic closure $I_{\mathrm{ion}}=I(V_m,\mathbf w)$,
$\mathrm d\mathbf w/\mathrm dt=\mathbf F(V_m,\mathbf w)$, and initial data
$V_m(\mathbf x,0)$, $\mathbf w(\mathbf x,0)$. cardiacFoam (`bidomainSolver`)
solves the system in the unknowns $V_m$ and $\phi_e$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\chi C_m \frac{\partial V_m}{\partial t}
&=\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m\right)
+\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_e\right)
-\chi C_m I_{\mathrm{ion}}+I_{\mathrm{app}},\\
\nabla\cdot\left((\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e)\nabla\phi_e\right)
&=-\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m\right)+s_e .
\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation with the two sealed walls is a pure Neumann problem:
$\phi_e$ is fixed up to a constant, and a solution exists only if
$\int_{\Omega_H} s_e\,\mathrm dV=0$. Every problem below prescribes the exact
fields at $t=0$ as initial data, and both sealed-wall conditions are satisfied
by the exact potentials themselves. The units are those of the monodomain
document: SI units for the continuum equations, and fields written in case
units on the normalised coordinates $x/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $t/(1\,\mathrm s)$.

## Manufactured ionic closure {#sec-ionic}

Both problems use the manufactured ionic model of
@pathmanathan2013verification, with state $(V_m,u_1,u_2,u_3)$. The solver
supplies $V_m$; the model advances the auxiliary states with $V_m$ held fixed,
at the rates

{{< include ../../latex/fda_rate_u1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/fda_rate_u2.tex >}}

and $\dot u_3=0$. The model returns

{{< include ../../latex/fda_Jion.tex >}}

and the solver divides it by $C_m$,

{{< include ../../latex/fda_Iion.tex >}}

The FDA cube uses the ionic model `bidomainFDAManufactured`, whose $\beta_d$ is
computed from the two conductivities (@sec-fda); the shell uses
`monodomainFDAManufactured` with the rounded $\beta=\beta_3=-8.6$ of the
monodomain document. With $u_3=0$ and auxiliary states that make
$(u_1-V_m)u_2^2=1/(1+t)$, the ionic term of the $V_m$ equation is

$$
-\chi C_m I_{\mathrm{ion}}=\chi C_m\,\frac{V_m}{2(1+t)}-\beta V_m ,
$$

which cancels the time derivative of $V_m=\sqrt{1+t}\,F$ and leaves
$-\beta V_m$.

## Gauge of the extracellular potential {#sec-gauge}

The exact potentials are defined up to a common constant $c$. Each problem
fixes $c$ by the value $\phi_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$ (`phiEReferenceValue`, 0 in
both tutorials) of the exact $\phi_e$ at the point $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$
(`phiERefPoint`); the solver sets the same value in the cell that contains
$\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The verifiers report two kinds of $\phi_e$ error.
The rows `phiE` and `phiI` (FDA cube) compare with the exact field of this
constant; their error contains the difference between the point value and the
value of the reference cell. The rows `phiE_gauge` and `phiI_gauge` compare
with the exact field shifted by the volume mean of the $\phi_e$ error,

$$
\bar e=\frac{\sum_c V_c\left(\phi_{e,c}-\phi_e(\mathbf x_c)\right)}{\sum_c V_c},
\qquad
\phi_e^{\mathrm{gauge}}=\phi_e+\bar e,\quad
\phi_i^{\mathrm{gauge}}=\phi_i+\bar e ,
$$

with $V_c$ and $\mathbf x_c$ the volume and centre of cell $c$; the gauge rows
do not depend on $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Every error norm is volume
weighted: $L_1=\sum_cV_c|e_c|/\sum_cV_c$,
$L_2=(\sum_cV_ce_c^2/\sum_cV_c)^{1/2}$, $L_\infty=\max_c|e_c|$.

## Reading and regenerating {#sec-regenerate}

The generators live in `tutorials/manufacturedSolutions/generators/` of the
cardiacFoam repository. Each problem has one sympy generator `<case>_mms.py`
that writes

- `reference/<case>.py`, a NumPy-only module with the exact fields and
  sources;
- `latex/<case>_*.tex`, the fragments printed in this document.

Set up the environment once and run a generator from that folder:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python fda_bidomain_mms.py --emit
.venv/bin/python fda_bidomain_mms.py --self-check
```

`--emit` runs the self-checks first and writes nothing if one fails;
`--self-check` runs them alone. `shell_bidomain_mms.py` also takes
`--check PATH` and `--write PATH`, which compare or rewrite its C++ header and
are needed only by cardiacFoam developers. `docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py`
holds what depends on the tutorial cases: `--self-check` asserts that their
dictionaries carry the conductivities and reference points of the generators,
and `--run-check KIND=CASE ...` (`KIND` is `fda` or `shell`) compares the
exact fields with a finished run (@sec-fda-checks, @sec-shell-checks) and
writes nothing. The document is built with

```bash
quarto render docs/bidomain/bidomain_mms.qmd --to pdf
```

and its figures with `python docs/bidomain/figures.py`, which takes
`--draft`, `--outdir DIR` and `--mesh-case NAME=PATH` (names `fda_cube_hex`,
`fda_cube_tet`, `shell_hex`, `shell_tet`) as the monodomain figure script
does.

{{< include ../_common/creating.qmd >}}

# FDA cube {#sec-fda}

## Description and limitations

The bidomain problem of @pathmanathan2013verification, part of the FDA
regulatory science tool for cardiac electrophysiology [@fda2023eprst], on the
unit cube $[0,1]^d$, $d=1,2,3$. The transmembrane potential is the FDA
monodomain field and the extracellular potential is a fixed multiple of it.
The case exercises the elliptic $\phi_e$ solve, the parabolic $V_m$ solve,
their coupling through $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_e)$ and
$\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m)$, the gauge of $\phi_e$, the ionic coupling
and the time integration, on hexahedra in one, two and three dimensions and on
Delaunay tetrahedra in three.

Both tensors are diagonal and $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ is proportional to $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$,
so $\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ is a multiple of $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$, $\phi_e$ is a
multiple of $V_m$ at every time and the elliptic equation needs no source.
The exact field has a zero normal derivative on every face and the face
normals are eigenvectors of both tensors, so both conormal fluxes vanish
because of the field. The case therefore does not exercise unequal anisotropy
ratios, off-diagonal conductivity, a $\phi_e$ source or its compatibility, or
a wall flux reconstruction; the sealed shell (@sec-shell) does.

The residual of the equations is not zero. The tutorial dictionary gives
$\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ to the nine decimals of $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$, so the ratio
$\sigma_{i,mm}/(\sigma_{i,mm}+\sigma_{e,mm})$ equals $\kappa$ to about $10^{-9}$ on the $y$
and $z$ axes and exactly on the $x$ axis. On the exact fields the residuals of
the $V_m$ and $\phi_e$ equations are $\rho_pV_m$ and $\rho_eV_m$ (both written
as left minus right side of the forms above), with

$$
\rho_p=\sum_{m=1}^{d}\left((1-\kappa)\sigma_{i,mm}-H_{mm}\right)(m\pi)^2,
\qquad
\rho_e=\sum_{m=1}^{d}\left(\kappa\,(\sigma_{i,mm}+\sigma_{e,mm})-\sigma_{i,mm}\right)(m\pi)^2 ,
$$

and relative to $k_d$, the size of $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m)/V_m$,

{{< include ../../latex/fda_bidomain_residual_relative.tex >}}

In cardiacFoam:

- tutorial `manufacturedSolutions/bidomain`, options `-dim 1|2|3`
  (`-mesh hex`, the default) and `-mesh tet` (three dimensions);
- myocardium solver `bidomainSolver` (`sealedHeartBoundary false`,
  `conductivitySource uniform`);
- ionic model `bidomainFDAManufactured`, which rejects tensors with mixed
  entries between active directions and ratios
  $\sigma_{i,mm}/(\sigma_{i,mm}+\sigma_{e,mm})$ that differ from $\kappa$ by more than
  $10^{-6}\kappa$;
- verifier `manufacturedFDABidomainVerifier`.

## Construction

The spatial factor $F_d$ of the FDA monodomain problem is an eigenfunction of
the diagonal operator, $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla F_d)=-k_dF_d$ with

{{< include ../../latex/fda_bidomain_kd.tex >}}

($\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ is the conductivity of the monodomain FDA problem, so $k_d$ is
the eigenvalue of that document). With $\phi_e=-\kappa V_m+c$ and
$\kappa(\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e)=\boldsymbol\sigma_i$,

$$
\nabla\cdot\left(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m\right)
+\nabla\cdot\left((\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e)\nabla\phi_e\right)
=\nabla\cdot\left((\boldsymbol\sigma_i-\kappa(\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e))\nabla V_m\right)=0 ,
$$

so the elliptic equation holds with $s_e=0$. In the $V_m$ equation
$\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i)=(1-\kappa)\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m)
=-(1-\kappa)k_dV_m$, and $(1-\kappa)\sigma_{i,mm}=H_{mm}$, the harmonic combination
of the two diagonals. The ionic model sets

{{< include ../../latex/fda_bidomain_beta.tex >}}

so that $-\beta_dV_m$ from the ionic term (@sec-ionic) cancels the diffusion
term and no applied current is needed ($I_{\mathrm{app}}=0$). The constant $c$
makes $\phi_e(\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}},t)=\phi_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$ at every time:

{{< include ../../latex/fda_bidomain_c.tex >}}

## Self-checks {#sec-fda-checks}

`fda_bidomain_mms.py --self-check` asserts, for $d=1,2,3$, in exact rational
arithmetic on the decimals of the conductivities:

- $\partial_tu_1$ and $\partial_tu_2$ equal the ionic rates on the exact fields;
- the residuals of both equations are constant multiples $\rho_pV_m$,
  $\rho_eV_m$ of $V_m$ with $|\rho_p|/k_d\le10^{-8}$ and
  $|\rho_e|/k_d\le10^{-8}$ (the values are printed above);
- $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla V_m$, $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla\phi_e$
  and $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i$ vanish on every face;
- $\phi_e(\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}},t)=\phi_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$;
- the ratios $\sigma_{i,mm}/(\sigma_{i,mm}+\sigma_{e,mm})$ agree with $\kappa$ to
  $10^{-6}\kappa$, the tolerance of the ionic model;
- the printed constants round-trip.

`docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py --self-check` asserts that the
conductivities and `phiERefPoint` of the tutorial `constant/electroProperties`
equal those of the generator.

*Comparison with a run.* `bidomain_reference.py --run-check fda=CASE` reads
the cell centres and volumes (from `constant/polyMesh`, by the face-triangle and face-pyramid
decomposition OpenFOAM uses), the computed `Vm` and `phiE` of the last time and
`postProcessing/<d>D_<n>_cells.dat`, and recomputes from the exact fields above
the `Vm`, `phiE`, `phiE_gauge` and `phiI_gauge` norms and $\bar e$. On the
runs `1D_N10`, `2D_N10` and `3D_N10` of the study `cartesianConvergence`
($t=0.2$) all agree with the reported values to the six printed digits, and the
written initial `preProcess_u1` equals $u_1(\mathbf x_c,0)$ to $2\times10^{-15}$.

## Regeneration

```bash
python fda_bidomain_mms.py --emit
python fda_bidomain_mms.py --self-check
python docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py --self-check
R=../bidomain/setup/studies/cartesianConvergence/results
python docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py --run-check fda=$R/3D_N10
```

`--emit` writes `reference/fda_bidomain.py` and `latex/fda_bidomain_*.tex`.
The spatial factors, the auxiliary states and the ionic closure are those of
`fda_monodomain_mms.py`, imported. The bidomain functions of cardiacFoam
(`manufacturedFDABidomainReference.H` and the constants of
`bidomainFDAManufactured.C`) are hand-written and carry no generated regions,
so the generator has no `--check`; the run comparison above is the
comparison.

# Sealed spherical shell {#sec-shell}

## Description and limitations

The heart-like shell $r_1<|\mathbf x|<r_2$ of the monodomain document, both
spheres sealed, with two full intracellular and extracellular tensors whose
fibre and sheet rotate through the wall. The tensors share one orthonormal
frame but have unequal eigenvalue ratios, so $\boldsymbol\sigma_i+\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ is not
a multiple of $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$, and both are oblique to both walls. The exact
$\phi_i$ and $\phi_e$ have non-zero normal and tangential gradients on both
walls while $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla\phi_i$ and
$\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla\phi_e$ vanish there exactly. The case
exercises the sealed-wall operators of both potentials on curved walls, a
non-trivial $\phi_e$ source with zero integral, the pure Neumann $\phi_e$
system with its gauge and compatibility, and spatially varying tensors whose
derivatives enter both sources.

It does not exercise a bath, the ECG, a stimulus or a wall that carries
current, and the two tensors have the same principal axes everywhere, so a
discretisation error that appears only when the eigenvectors of $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$
and $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ differ is not detected.

## Problem instance

The parameters are

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_params.tex >}}

with $\chi=3$, $C_m=2$, and the gauge and reaction coefficient

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_ref.tex >}}

The inner sphere is the patch `endocardium` and the outer sphere the patch
`epicardium`. In cardiacFoam:

- tutorial `manufacturedSolutions/bidomain/sphericalShell`, options
  `-mesh hex|tet` and `-N`;
- myocardium solver `bidomainSolver` (`sealedHeartBoundary true`,
  `conductivitySource field`, the cell tensors written by
  `setManufacturedFields` to `0/ConductivityIntracellular` and
  `0/ConductivityExtracellular`);
- ionic model `monodomainFDAManufactured` (`dimension "3D"`);
- verifier `manufacturedShellBidomainVerifier`, which adds $I_{\mathrm{app}}$
  and $s_e$ and requests the compatibility projection of the $\phi_e$ system.

## Construction

*Transmural coordinate and conductivities.* The coordinate $\lambda$, the
fibre angle $\theta$, the fixed frame $(\mathbf e_a,\mathbf e_b,\mathbf n_s)$,
the fibre $\mathbf f$ and the sheet $\mathbf s$ are those of the monodomain
shell:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_lambda.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_theta.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_frame.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_fibre.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_sheet.tex >}}

Both tensors are built on this frame with their own eigenvalues:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Gi.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Ge.tex >}}

$\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ is the conductivity $\boldsymbol\sigma$ of the monodomain shell.
The eigenvalue ratios are $17:1.9:1$ for $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ and $7.75:1.5:1$ for
$\boldsymbol\sigma_e$.

*Sealing.* Each potential is sealed with respect to its own tensor by the
construction of the monodomain shell. $\omega$ vanishes on both spheres, with
normal derivative $d_j$ on sphere $j$ and $\mathbf n_j$ the unit normal out of
the heart:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_omega.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_n2.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d1.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_d2.tex >}}

For the intracellular factor, with $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$,

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_mj_i.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_m_i.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Fi.tex >}}

and for the extracellular factor, with $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$,

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_mj_e.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_m_e.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Fe.tex >}}

so that $\mathbf n_j\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla F_i=0$ and
$\mathbf n_j\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla F_e=0$ on both spheres. $F_i$ equals the
field $F$ of the monodomain shell.

*Potentials and gauge.* $\phi_i=\sqrt{1+t}\,F_i+c$ and
$\phi_e=\sqrt{1+t}\,F_e+c$, so $V_m=\sqrt{1+t}\,(F_i-F_e)$ carries no constant,
and $c$ makes $\phi_e(\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}},t)=\phi_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_c.tex >}}

*Ionic closure and sources.* The auxiliary states use the positive function
$g$ of the monodomain shell, so the ionic rates hold exactly and the ionic term
leaves $-\beta V_m$ in the $V_m$ equation (@sec-ionic). The applied current is
the remainder of the $V_m$ equation and $s_e$ is the residual of the $\phi_e$
equation with no source:

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_Is.tex >}}

{{< include ../../latex/shell_bidomain_se.tex >}}

Both fluxes $\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla F_i$ and $\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla F_e$ have zero
normal component on both spheres, so by the divergence theorem
$\int_{\Omega_H} s_e\,\mathrm dV=0$: the $\phi_e$ problem is compatible in the
continuum. The divergences include the derivatives of the spatially varying
tensors.

## Self-checks {#sec-shell-checks}

`shell_bidomain_mms.py --self-check` asserts:

- sealing: $\max|\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla F_i|$ and
  $\max|\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma_e\nabla F_e|$ below $10^{-25}$ at 200 points of
  each sphere, in 30-digit arithmetic on the exact sphere;
- sources: both divergences agree with central differences of the fluxes to
  $10^{-6}$ at 40 points of the shell;
- positivity: every $\mathbf n_j\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\,\mathbf n_j>0$ and $g>0.5$ over
  4000 points of the shell widened by 0.05 on each side;
- richness of the walls: on each wall the means of the tangential parts of
  $\boldsymbol\sigma_i\mathbf n/\sigma_{i,f}$, $\boldsymbol\sigma_e\mathbf n/\sigma_{e,f}$,
  $\nabla F_i$, $\nabla F_e$ and $\nabla(F_i-F_e)$ exceed $10^{-2}$;
- compatibility: the Gauss--Legendre integral of
  $s_e/\sqrt{1+t}$ over the shell ($60\times60$ points in $|\mathbf x|$ and
  $\cos\vartheta$, 120 in the azimuth) is below $10^{-12}$ times the integral
  of its absolute value;
- $F_i$ equals the monodomain shell field to $10^{-13}$ at 200 points;
- $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ and $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ commute to $10^{-14}$ (one frame) at 500
  points, and the relative distance of $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ from the multiples of
  $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ is at least 0.1 at every point (it is 0.104 at least);
- $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ equals $\boldsymbol\sigma$ of `shell_monodomain_mms.py`;
- the residual of the $V_m$ equation and of the two ionic rates vanish
  symbolically, with $F_i$, $F_e$, $g$, $\beta$ and
  $\nabla\cdot(\boldsymbol\sigma_i\nabla F_i)$ as symbols;
- the reference point $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{ref}}$ lies inside the shell.

`docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py --self-check` asserts that `phiERefPoint`
and the ionic model of the tutorial equal those of the generator.

*Comparison with a run.* `bidomain_reference.py --run-check shell=CASE`
recomputes, from the cell centres and volumes of `constant/polyMesh`, the tensors and the `Vm` and
`phiE_gauge` norms of a finished run and compares them with
`0/ConductivityIntracellular`, `0/ConductivityExtracellular` and
`postProcessing/3D_<hex|tet>_<N>_cells.dat`. On the runs `sealed_hex_N8_s1`
(study `hexConvergence`) and `sealed_tet_N10_s1` (study `tetConvergence`),
both at $t=0.2$, the tensors agree to $3\times10^{-15}$ relative, the norms to
$5\times10^{-12}$ relative (12 printed digits), and `preProcess_u1` equals
$u_1(\mathbf x_c,0)$ to $10^{-15}$.

(c) The frame common to $\boldsymbol\sigma_i$ and $\boldsymbol\sigma_e$ at six sites through the wall on the cut face, the fibre shaded from the inner (light) to the outer (dark) wall, with the eigenvalues of each tensor along each direction.](figures/shell_bidomain.png){#fig-shell width=100%}

## Regeneration

```bash
python shell_bidomain_mms.py --emit
python shell_bidomain_mms.py --self-check
H=../../../src/verificationModels/bidomainVerification
python shell_bidomain_mms.py --check $H/manufacturedShellBidomainReference.H
R=../bidomain/sphericalShell/setup/studies/hexConvergence/results
python docs/bidomain/bidomain_reference.py --run-check shell=$R/sealed_hex_N8_s1
```

`--emit` writes `reference/shell_bidomain.py` and `latex/shell_bidomain_*.tex`;
the shared fragments `latex/shell_*.tex` are those of
`shell_monodomain_mms.py`. `--write` writes the whole cardiacFoam header,
including a table of self-test samples that the verifier compares with its
compiled functions at start-up.
